clue.text: Instruction for playing musical returned by censor

indicators.note: returned means the name of the musical is read backwards before the censor follows

parts.note: Cats is the long-running Lloyd Webber musical
Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and is known as Cato the Censor

explanation.surface: A score marking for a show that a censor sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns CATS into STAC; Cato the Censor then supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a direction on sheet music telling the player to make notes short and detached.

clue.text: The cane Pip didn't find so amusing

definitions.text: The cane Pip didn't find so amusing

parts.words: The cane Pip didn't find so amusing
parts.note: in Great Expectations the young hero is beaten by his sister with a cane she has given a jokey name, which suggests fun he never felt

explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Joe Gargery's cane in Dickens's Great Expectations is called Tickler; Pip found it anything but funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tickles amuses, but this cane's name was bitter irony for the boy it was used on.

clue.text: Flower begotten of man's penultimate age

explanation.surface: A bloom born in a man's declining years.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's sixth age of man is 'the lean and slippered pantaloon'; in the harlequinade, Columbine is Pantaloon's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbine is the aquilegia, a garden plant; it is also the name of the stock comedy heroine whose father is Pantaloon.

clue.text: Articles on. Mozart's first choral work

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the articles sit on top of the next piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Mozart's is taken

explanation.surface: Grammar words placed above the composer's debut piece for singers.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a piece of sacred music sung by a church choir.

clue.text: The 'tale of the dustman's fortune — one we both know

explanation.surface: A story about a refuse collector's riches, told by a shared acquaintance.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's last finished novel centres on Boffin, 'the Golden Dustman', who inherits a fortune made from dust heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's novel title; the phrase also names a person who is an acquaintance of both speakers.

clue.text: Like Mrs Siddons as Melpomene

parts.note: Sarah Siddons, the great actress, was painted by Reynolds posing as Melpomene, the Muse of the drama of sorrow

explanation.walkthrough: Reynolds's famous portrait is titled Mrs Siddons as the Tragic Muse; Melpomene is the Muse of tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Melpomene presides over tragedy, so an actress portrayed as her is cast in the sorrowful, dramatic mould.

clue.text: Area in which a couple of Poles perform

indicators.note: in which says the second part goes inside the word for area

parts.note: a tract is an area of land
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A region where two Polish people put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' wants to be Polish people; it means the geographic poles, N and S. 'in which' puts A plus NS inside TRACT after TR.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to carry out or conduct business, to see a deal through.

clue.text: A thousand dollars raised, almost without deduction lucrative!

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the two pieces are read upwards

parts.note: G, a grand, is slang for a thousand dollars

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: paid in full means paid without any deduction

explanation.surface: Raising a thousand dollars nearly without tax taken off is profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns A G into GA; 'almost' drops the final L of IN FULL to give INFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainful work earns money, so it is profitable or paying.

clue.text: Fruit to make tin soldiers look up

parts.note: a can is a tin container
TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Something to make toy soldiers glance upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin soldiers' looks like toys but splits into tin and soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloup is a variety of melon with orange flesh.

clue.text: The cat given by eastern commander to many

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A big cat handed over by an officer from the East to a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of the Americas, an example of the feline family.

clue.text: Sappers go to battle in response to stimulus

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers
action is fighting, a battle

explanation.surface: Army engineers march off to fight in answer to a provocation.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in Britain they form the Royal Engineers, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a physical or emotional reply prompted by some outside trigger.

clue.text: A torch for Father Brown's ex-jewel-thief

explanation.surface: A lamp belonging to G. K. Chesterton's clerical detective.
explanation.walkthrough: In Chesterton's Father Brown stories, Flambeau is the master jewel thief whom the priest reforms into a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch carried in processions; Chesterton named his reformed criminal after it.

clue.text: Man a location for Fingal's Cave

parts.note: to man a place is to staff it

explanation.surface: An instruction to crew the site of a famous Scottish sea cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a verb here, not a person. Fingal's Cave is a sea cave in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is the small Hebridean island whose basalt columns form the sea grotto that inspired Mendelssohn.

clue.text: Beastly sounding old rumour

indicators.note: sounding tells us the entry is spoken like the word for beastly

parts.note: brute as an adjective means beastly, animal-like

explanation.surface: A nasty-sounding piece of ancient gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruit is an archaic noun for a report or rumour spread about, hence old.

clue.text: Crafty rustic piper?

parts.note: read whimsically as of a craft, a boat's
a swain is a country youth

explanation.surface: A cunning country fellow who plays the pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: A bosun pipes orders on a whistle, hence the question-marked definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun uses a bosun's whistle, so he is a piper of sorts aboard ship.

clue.text: Correct procedure to' change coil input

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Proper practice for swapping out a coil in an electrical input.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctilio is a fine point of etiquette or proper conduct, scrupulous correctness.

clue.text: Gatecrashing ."'suitor .intoxicated in pub

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: intoxicated, i.e. drunk, signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunken admirer barging into a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intoxicated' rearranges SUITOR to TRUSIO, which 'in' puts between the two Ns of INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatecrashing is entering uninvited, an unwelcome entry.

clue.text: This minor crack means' end of British transport system

indicators.note: end of means just the final letter of British is used

parts.note: an airline is a system of air transport

explanation.surface: A small flaw spells the end of Britain's flight network.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline fracture is a very thin crack, as narrow as a single hair.

clue.text: Pleasing like Watts' nestlings:

explanation.surface: Charming, as the young birds in a hymn writer's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Watts wrote 'Birds in their little nests agree', so his nestlings are able to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable means pleasant to be with; read as agree-able it describes birds that get along.

clue.text: No one-day: builder, this fratricide.

parts.note: the city he founded was famously not built in a day, and he killed his twin brother

explanation.walkthrough: Rome wasn't built in a day; its legendary founder slew his brother Remus.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical founder of Rome murdered his twin, and his city took far longer than a day to build.

clue.text: It binds constituents to make a: return

indicators.note: make a return means the word for constituents goes back, read right to left

parts.note: constituents are parts of a whole

explanation.surface: A thing that ties components together to file a tax form.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a band of leather or fabric used to fasten or hold things together.

clue.text: Pistol, an old one

explanation.surface: A gun that is an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Henry plays the swaggerer Pistol is called Ancient Pistol, ancient meaning ensign.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Pistol holds the rank of ensign, once called an ancient; the word also means very old.

clue.text: In a poor district. Yorkist leader found refuge

indicators.note: In tells us the next pick sits inside the word made by a poor district

parts.note: a slum is a run-down poor area

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Yorkist

explanation.surface: A Wars of the Roses commander finds shelter in a shabby neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or shelter given to one who flees danger.

clue.text: Totter when hotter

explanation.surface: One who wobbles when the weather warms up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totter' is not staggering but one who tots up figures, i.e. adds them, a summer; the season is the hotter time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: One who adds sums up a column is someone doing arithmetic; the warm season comes between spring and autumn.

clue.text: Note well what is expedient

parts.note: re is the second note of the tonic sol-fa scale
a well is a spring or source

explanation.surface: Mark carefully what is the convenient thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note well' looks like the Latin nota bene instruction, but splits into note and well.
explanation.definitionFit: A resource is a means or stratagem to fall back on, something expedient in a difficulty.

clue.text: Invest a pound in special variety of pimento

indicators.note: to invest is to place money in, so the pound is put inside the rearranged letters
a variety of something is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Put a pound into a special type of pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges SPECIAL to ALSPICE, and 'Invest' puts L inside it after the first L.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is the dried berry of the pimento tree, so the two names are used for the same spice.

clue.text: Hang around like. Keats's: knight at arms

explanation.surface: Linger, as the knight in a Romantic ballad does.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's La Belle Dame sans Merci asks what ails the knight-at-arms, 'Alone and palely loitering'.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly; Keats's knight is pictured doing just that by a withered lake.

clue.text: How eg feet fit comfortably in; honest leather

indicators.note: in tells us the entry is tucked inside the run of the words honest leather

explanation.surface: Feet sit snugly in good honest leather shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly and cosily into a place.

clue.text: Rule made into new form

indicators.note: put into new form means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regulation rewritten in a different shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to hold sway or have control over, to govern.
